# 3. Execution layer: how it acts

[← Home](../README.md) · [The stack](README.md) · [Data layer](data.md) · [Agent layer](agent.md) · **Execution layer** · [Harness layer](harness.md) · [Application layer](application.md)

> **How does a decision become a fill, safely?**

**Scope.** Broker and venue tools that give an agent order authority, trading engines that run the same code in backtest and live, and pipelines that turn target weights into orders.

**Where it usually breaks:** an agent with an order tool and no guard; retries that double-submit; state lost on a crash; no reconciliation between intent and fills.

**Open gap.** No catalogued paper is about execution for LLM agents. Most agent projects stop at a decision; the order path, limits and reconciliation are left to you.

## Builder notes

Recommendations from this list's maintainers, distilled from the sources above. They are design advice, not results reported by those sources.

- **Reconcile before you resend.** When an order's state is unknown after a timeout or crash, reconcile with the broker first; never blindly resend. Keep intent, checkpoint and replay separate from the real side effects, and do not promise exactly-once delivery.
- **Charting access is not order authority.** Connecting an agent to a charting or data platform does not grant it broker execution. Start every connector read-only, review each tool and session permission, and enable write tools one at a time on a paper account.
